audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Joshua / Yehoshua Ai ambush, king execution, Ebal altar, and public Torah-reading narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for renewed courage, plunder permission, ambush instructions, thirty-thousand/five-thousand figures, destruction of Ai, king hanging and burial, Mount Ebal altar, Torah inscription, Gerizim/Ebal assembly, and inclusive public reading.

verses.restored: YHWH said to Joshua, Do not fear and do not be shattered. Take with you all people of war, rise and go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Joshua, Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the people of war with thee, and arise, go up to Ai: see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land:

verses.restored: You shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king; only its spoil and livestock you may plunder for yourselves. Set for yourself an ambush for city from behind it.

familiar.text: And thou shalt do to Ai and her king as thou didst unto Jericho and her king: only the spoil thereof, and the cattle thereof, shall ye take for a prey unto yourselves: lay thee an ambush for the city behind it.

verses.restored: Joshua rose and all people of war to go up to Ai; Joshua chose thirty thousand men, mighty ones of strength, and sent them by night.

familiar.text: So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up against Ai: and Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour, and sent them away by night.

verses.restored: He commanded them, saying, See, you shall lie in ambush for city from behind city. Do not be very far from city, and all of you be ready.

familiar.text: And he commanded them, saying, Behold, ye shall lie in wait against the city, even behind the city: go not very far from the city, but be ye all ready:

verses.restored: I and all people who are with me will draw near to city. It shall be, when they come out to meet us as at first, that we will flee before them.

familiar.text: And I, and all the people that are with me, will approach unto the city: and it shall come to pass, when they come out against us, as at the first, that we will flee before them,

verses.restored: They will come out after us until we draw them away from city, for they will say, They are fleeing before us as at first; and we will flee before them.

familiar.text: (For they will come out after us) till we have drawn them from the city; for they will say, They flee before us, as at the first: therefore we will flee before them.

verses.restored: Then you shall rise from ambush and possess city, and YHWH your Divine will give it into your hand.

familiar.text: Then ye shall rise up from the ambush, and seize upon the city: for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.

verses.restored: It shall be, when you capture city, you shall set city on fire; according to word of YHWH you shall do. See, I have commanded you.

familiar.text: And it shall be, when ye have taken the city, that ye shall set the city on fire: according to the commandment of the LORD shall ye do. See, I have commanded you.

verses.restored: Joshua sent them, and they went to place of ambush and dwelt between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai; and Joshua lodged that night in midst of people.

familiar.text: Joshua therefore sent them forth: and they went to lie in ambush, and abode between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai: but Joshua lodged that night among the people.

verses.restored: Joshua rose early in morning and mustered people, and he and elders of Israel went up before people to Ai.

familiar.text: And Joshua rose up early in the morning, and numbered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.

familiar.text: And all the people, even the people of war that were with him, went up, and drew nigh, and came before the city, and pitched on the north side of Ai: now there was a valley between them and Ai.

verses.restored: He took about five thousand men and set them as ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of city.

familiar.text: And he took about five thousand men, and set them to lie in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city.

familiar.text: And when they had set the people, even all the host that was on the north of the city, and their liers in wait on the west of the city, Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley.

verses.restored: It was, when king of Ai saw, that men of city hurried and rose early and went out to meet Israel for battle, he and all his people, at appointed place before Arabah; but he did not know there was an ambush against him behind city.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the king of Ai saw it, that they hasted and rose up early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at a time appointed, before the plain; but he wist not that there were liers in ambush against him behind the city.

translation_notes: The chapter repeats Jericho's total-war pattern while permitting Israel to keep livestock and spoil, a change that follows the Achan crisis but does not make the conquest ethical.
Verses 3 and 12 give thirty-thousand and five-thousand ambush forces. These may describe separate detachments, compositional layers, or textual difficulties and require witness comparison.
Verse 17 includes Bethel in the Masoretic text, though narrative and textual questions remain about its role in the battle.
The ambush uses feigned retreat, an undefended city, fire, encirclement, and denial of escape. The text reports no survivor and twelve thousand dead, including women.
The king is hanged and then removed at sunset, continuing Deuteronomy's same-day burial limit even for an enemy ruler.
Ai's archaeological identification and occupation history are disputed; the narrative must not be presented as uncomplicated archaeological fact.
The Ebal altar and Torah inscription link conquest to Deuteronomy 27, but textual traditions differ regarding altar location, especially the Samaritan Pentateuch's Gerizim reading.

The closing public reading includes leaders, native-born residents, immigrants, women, and children. This inclusive access to Torah is a constructive thread that does not erase the preceding massacre.
safety_note: Never use Joshua 8 to justify ambush warfare against civilians, genocide, city burning, looting, execution, territorial conquest, or archaeological overclaiming. Keep Ai's dead visible while preserving the chapter's better closing movement: public Torah, shared assembly, peace offerings, and equal hearing for women, children, immigrants, leaders, and ordinary residents.
